content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The UK's Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC) has withdrawn all funding for e-MERLIN, the network of radio telescopes operated from Jodrell Bank Observatory, putting the historic Lovell Telescope at risk of closure, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/science/2026/07/28/signals_are_grim_for_jodrell_bank_observatory_after_uk_science_funding_decision/5279451). The cut is part of a wider budget settlement STFC announced on 27 July 2026 for its Particle P...

recommendations: Add ras.ac.uk and ukri.org to config/source_allowlist.txt -- both are legitimate primary/official sources (Royal Astronomical Society; UK Research and Innovation) that should not need per-article override in future submissions.
No corrections record required -- no factual, attribution, or quote issue was found in this article.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (852 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. The Analysis section adds genuine editorial value by explicitly naming the tension between the 2.7% PPAN headline figure and the fact that e-MERLIN absorbs a full funding withdrawal within that figure -- a distinction the RAS's own statement invites ('cautiously welcomed... before the facility-level detail... emerged') rather than one invented by the bot.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 cited sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and snapshotted to sources/2026-07/uk-slashes-astronomy-funding-putting-jodrell-banks-lovell-telescope-and-e-merlin-at-risk-of-closure/. I independently re-hashed each gunzipped snapshot and confirmed the sha256 matched manifest.json exactly for all three (source-0: 275d717a298dff997a0644241dcaf40cfe900b51abe7ff094e24c12617a9dc0a; source-1: de7afb5357b67f56837f48752ea587e420cc0f831239bb1029e05bb575e6220f; source-2: 969584304b857d940e3a893cee6996fc3b41e93f77e68e398b0c0b759c8f12c0) -- no live WebFetch was needed since every snapshot saved cleanly. I then read the full extracted text of each: (1) source-0.html.gz, theregister.com -- confirms the 2.7% PPAN cut over four years, e-MERLIN funding ending 2028, the 250-foot Lovell dish turning 70 next year and Grade I-listed status, the JCMT withdrawal, BiSON facing a cut to 60% of prior funding (=40% cut), and verbatim quotes from Jim Wild, Michele Dougherty ('tough, but necessary, decisions'), the Jodrell Bank spokesperson, Brian Cox, and MP Tim Roca. (2) source-1.html.gz, ras.ac.uk -- confirms, verbatim, 'STFC is withdrawing all funding for e-MERLIN... a group of seven UK radio telescopes including the iconic Lovell Telescope,' the JCMT withdrawal, the 20% SKA Regional Centre cut, the Vera Rubin Telescope cuts, the 40% BISON cut, the previously-feared 30% PPAN cut, the 2.7% headline figure, the 10% instrument-cut expectation, and both full Jim Wild quotes reproduced exactly as quoted in the article. This is the single source that supports the article's central 2.7%-vs-full-withdrawal distinction, and it does so explicitly and unambiguously. (3) source-2.html.gz, ukri.org -- confirms, verbatim, the 2.7% PPAN four-year decrease, the flat core budget 2026-2030 following 'a record settlement... in the 2025 Spending Review,' the four named cost pressures (energy, FX, staffing, expanded portfolio), the 27 July 2026 dateline, and the full Michele Dougherty quote reproduced word-for-word in the article. I confirmed by keyword search that this UKRI page does NOT name Jodrell Bank or e-MERLIN anywhere in its body text, which directly substantiates the article's 'What We Don't Know' claim that STFC's own announcement did not name individual facilities.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked traces to a cited source: the 2.7% headline figure (UKRI + RAS), the full e-MERLIN funding withdrawal (RAS, verbatim), the 2028 funding cliff (Register), the 20%/40%/30%/10% figures (RAS, verbatim), the Lovell Telescope's dimensions/age/listing (Register), and all six direct quotes (Wild x2, Dougherty x2 combined into one attributed quote, Jodrell Bank spokesperson, Brian Cox) reproduce their sources exactly, character for character, with no paraphrase-inside-quote-marks and no misattribution. The headline funding-figure distinction the task flagged as a specific risk -- '2.7% headline cut' vs. 'full e-MERLIN funding withdrawal' -- is not conflated anywhere in the article: the 2.7% figure is consistently attributed to UKRI/RAS as the PPAN-wide aggregate, and the e-MERLIN full-withdrawal fact is consistently and correctly sourced to RAS alone, matching the RAS press release's own framing precisely.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout. Every claim carries an explicit 'according to X' attribution. Quotes from campaigners/critics (Cox, RAS) and from the funding body (STFC's Dougherty) are both represented, giving the piece appropriate balance for a contentious funding story without editorializing.
